description: A Python CLI that ingests job ads, analyzes them with Claude API, tailors a master CV to match, and generates a stylish ATS-optimized PDF in English or French.

userStories.title: Project Scaffolding
userStories.description: Set up the project structure with all necessary directories, configuration files, dependency management, master CV data file, and gitignore so that the codebase is ready for feature development.
acceptanceCriteria: pyproject.toml exists with all dependencies listed (anthropic, click, pydantic, python-dotenv, weasyprint, jinja2, beautifulsoup4, lxml, PyMuPDF, requests, langdetect, python-jobspy, playwright, pytest)
Directory structure created: src/, src/scraper/, src/analyzer/, src/tailor/, src/generator/, src/utils/, data/, tests/, tests/fixtures/, output/
All __init__.py files are present in src/ and its subdirectories
src/config.py loads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from .env via python-dotenv and exposes a Settings pydantic model

data/master_cv.json exists with a complete bilingual master CV including personal info, summary, experience (with parent/child structure), skills (categorized), education, languages, and certifications
.gitignore includes output/, .env, __pycache__/, *.pyc, .pytest_cache/, dist/, *.egg-info/
Running 'python -c "from src.config import Settings"' succeeds without error
userStories.notes: Foundation story. All other stories depend on this. master_cv.json must have realistic data with bilingual en/fr fields and id references.

userStories.title: Pydantic Data Models
userStories.description: Define the core Pydantic models for JobRequirements and TailoredCV that serve as the contracts between the analyzer, tailor, and generator modules.
acceptanceCriteria: src/analyzer/models.py defines JobRequirements with fields: title, company, location, required_skills (list), preferred_skills (list), experience_years (optional int), responsibilities (list), language (str), raw_text (str)

src/tailor/models.py defines TailoredCV with fields matching the master CV structure but with selected/reordered content: personal_info, summary (BilingualText), experience (list of TailoredExperience), skills (categorized dict), education, languages, certifications
BilingualText model exists with 'en' and 'fr' string fields and is reused across both modules
All models use strict Pydantic v2 syntax with model_config and field validators where appropriate
Unit tests in tests/test_models.py validate model creation, serialization, and validation error handling
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_models.py -x -v
userStories.notes: These models are the inter-module contracts. Analyzer produces JobRequirements; Tailor consumes JobRequirements + MasterCV and produces TailoredCV; Generator consumes TailoredCV.

userStories.title: File Scraper
userStories.description: Implement a file-based scraper that can extract text content from local PDF, HTML, and TXT job ad files.
acceptanceCriteria: src/scraper/file_scraper.py exposes a function scrape_file(path: Path) -> str that returns extracted text
PDF extraction uses PyMuPDF (fitz) to extract text from all pages
HTML extraction uses BeautifulSoup to strip tags and return clean text
TXT files are read directly with UTF-8 encoding
Raises a clear ValueError for unsupported file types
Unit tests in tests/test_file_scraper.py cover PDF, HTML, TXT, and unsupported formats using fixture files in tests/fixtures/
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_file_scraper.py -x -v
userStories.notes: Create minimal test fixture files (sample.pdf, sample.html, sample.txt) in tests/fixtures/. PDF fixture can be generated programmatically in test setup.

userStories.title: URL Scraper
userStories.description: Implement a URL scraper that fetches job ad content from web pages, with Playwright fallback for JavaScript-rendered content.
acceptanceCriteria: src/scraper/url_scraper.py exposes async function scrape_url(url: str) -> str
First attempts a simple requests.get with appropriate headers and timeout
If content looks empty or JS-heavy, falls back to Playwright for full rendering
HTML is parsed with BeautifulSoup to extract meaningful text (strips nav, footer, ads)
Raises ConnectionError or TimeoutError with descriptive messages on failure
Unit tests in tests/test_url_scraper.py mock both requests and playwright, testing success and fallback scenarios
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_url_scraper.py -x -v
userStories.notes: All network calls must be mocked in tests. Playwright is optional — code should handle ImportError gracefully if playwright is not installed.

userStories.title: Board Scraper
userStories.description: Implement a job board scraper that searches LinkedIn, Indeed, and Glassdoor via the python-jobspy library and returns matching job listings.
acceptanceCriteria: src/scraper/board_scraper.py exposes function scrape_boards(query: str, location: str, num_results: int = 5) -> list[dict]
Uses python-jobspy to search across supported job boards
Returns a list of dicts with keys: title, company, location, url, description
Handles jobspy exceptions gracefully and returns partial results if some boards fail
Accepts optional site_name parameter to restrict search to specific boards
Unit tests in tests/test_board_scraper.py mock the jobspy scrape function and test normal and error scenarios
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_board_scraper.py -x -v
userStories.notes: JobSpy returns a pandas DataFrame. Convert to list of dicts for downstream use. Mock the jobspy.scrape call in tests.

userStories.title: Language Detection Utility
userStories.description: Implement a language detection utility that identifies whether a job ad is in English or French, used to determine the output language of the tailored CV.
acceptanceCriteria: src/utils/language.py exposes function detect_language(text: str) -> str returning 'en' or 'fr'
Uses langdetect library with deterministic seeding for reproducible results
Falls back to 'en' if detection confidence is low or language is unsupported
Handles empty or very short text gracefully without crashing
Unit tests in tests/test_language.py test English text, French text, empty text, and mixed-language text
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_language.py -x -v
userStories.notes: Use langdetect.DetectorFactory.seed = 0 for deterministic results. Only support en/fr; map other detected languages to 'en'.

userStories.title: Job Analyzer
userStories.description: Implement the job analyzer that sends scraped job text to the Claude API and extracts structured JobRequirements from the response.
acceptanceCriteria: src/analyzer/analyzer.py exposes async function analyze_job(text: str, client: anthropic.Anthropic | None = None) -> JobRequirements
Sends a structured prompt to Claude API asking for JSON extraction of job requirements
Uses claude-sonnet-4-20250514 model for cost-effectiveness
Parses Claude's JSON response into a JobRequirements Pydantic model
Handles API errors (rate limit, auth, network) with descriptive error messages
Client parameter allows dependency injection for testing
Unit tests in tests/test_analyzer.py mock the anthropic client and test successful parsing and error handling
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_analyzer.py -x -v
userStories.notes: The prompt should instruct Claude to return valid JSON matching the JobRequirements schema. Include the schema description in the prompt for best results.

userStories.title: CV Tailor Core
userStories.description: Implement the core CV tailoring engine that rewrites the summary, enhances bullet points, and reorders skills based on job requirements.
acceptanceCriteria: src/tailor/tailor.py exposes async function tailor_cv(job: JobRequirements, master_cv: dict, language: str, client: anthropic.Anthropic | None = None) -> TailoredCV
Rewrites the professional summary to align with the target job, in the detected language
Enhances experience bullet points to emphasize relevant keywords from the job requirements
Reorders skills to place job-relevant skills first within each category
Never invents fake experiences, companies, or skills not present in master_cv.json
Client parameter allows dependency injection for testing
Unit tests in tests/test_tailor.py mock Claude API calls and verify output structure matches TailoredCV model
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_tailor.py -x -v
userStories.notes: The tailor uses Claude API for summary rewriting and bullet enhancement, but uses rule-based logic for skill reordering. Must preserve all real data from master CV.

userStories.title: Experience Selection Strategy
userStories.description: Implement rule-based experience selection and ranking that chooses the most relevant experiences from the master CV based on job requirements.
acceptanceCriteria: src/tailor/strategy.py exposes function select_experiences(job: JobRequirements, experiences: list[dict]) -> list[dict]
Scores each experience based on keyword overlap with job required_skills and responsibilities
Handles parent/child experience structure (Capgemini umbrella with sub-projects)
Returns experiences sorted by relevance score, with a configurable max count (default 5)
Preserves the original experience data without modification, only selects and orders
Unit tests in tests/test_strategy.py test scoring logic, parent/child handling, and max count limiting
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_strategy.py -x -v
userStories.notes: This is pure Python logic, no API calls. Keyword matching should be case-insensitive and handle partial matches. Parent experience inherits relevance from its children.

userStories.title: PDF Generator with Stylish Sidebar Layout
userStories.description: Implement the PDF generator using Jinja2 HTML templates and WeasyPrint to produce a stylish, ATS-optimized CV with a sidebar layout.
acceptanceCriteria: src/generator/generator.py exposes function generate_pdf(cv: TailoredCV, output_path: Path, language: str = 'en') -> Path
Uses a Jinja2 HTML template stored in src/generator/templates/cv_template.html
CSS creates a two-column layout: main content area (70%) + colored sidebar (30%) with contact info, skills, languages, certifications
Typography uses professional fonts (system fonts with web-safe fallbacks)
ATS-friendly: real text (not images), proper heading hierarchy, semantic HTML
Output PDF is saved to the specified output_path and the path is returned
Unit tests in tests/test_generator.py mock WeasyPrint and verify HTML generation and template rendering
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_generator.py -x -v
userStories.notes: WeasyPrint can be tricky on Windows. Tests should mock the WeasyPrint HTML().write_pdf() call. Focus on verifying the HTML output is correct.

userStories.title: Photo Integration in PDF
userStories.description: Add support for embedding a circular profile photo in the PDF sidebar, with graceful fallback when no photo is available.
acceptanceCriteria: src/generator/generator.py accepts an optional photo_path parameter
Photo is embedded as base64 data URI in the HTML template to avoid file path issues in WeasyPrint
CSS applies circular crop (border-radius: 50%) and appropriate sizing (120x120px)
When no photo is provided, the photo area is hidden cleanly without layout breakage
Supports JPEG and PNG image formats
Unit tests verify base64 encoding of photo and fallback behavior when photo is absent
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_generator.py -x -v
userStories.notes: Use base64 encoding to embed photos directly in the HTML. This avoids WeasyPrint file path resolution issues on Windows.

userStories.title: CLI Wiring and Full Pipeline
userStories.description: Wire all modules together through the Click CLI entry point, creating the complete pipeline from job input to PDF output.
acceptanceCriteria: src/main.py uses Click to define a CLI with commands: generate (from file/URL), search (from job boards), and version
generate command accepts --input (file path or URL), --language (en/fr/auto), --output (output path), --photo (optional photo path)
search command accepts --query, --location, --sites, --num-results and displays results for user selection
Full pipeline works: input → scrape → analyze → tailor → generate PDF
Proper error handling with user-friendly messages for missing API key, network errors, file not found
Unit tests in tests/test_cli.py use Click's CliRunner to test command invocations with mocked pipeline
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -x -v
userStories.notes: The CLI is the orchestration layer. It should import and call the other modules, not duplicate their logic. Use Click groups for sub-commands.

userStories.title: End-to-End Integration Test
userStories.description: Create an end-to-end integration test that exercises the full pipeline from job ad input to PDF generation with all external calls mocked.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_integration.py contains a full pipeline test from file input to PDF output
All external calls are mocked: Claude API returns realistic mock responses, WeasyPrint generates a mock PDF
Test verifies the entire data flow: scrape → analyze → tailor → generate
Test validates that the output TailoredCV contains only data from the master CV (no hallucinated content)
Test runs in both 'en' and 'fr' language modes
Test is marked with @pytest.mark.integration but runs by default (not skipped)
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_integration.py -x -v
userStories.notes: This is a smoke test for the full pipeline. All mocks should return plausible data. The test should catch integration issues between modules.

userStories.title: README Documentation
userStories.description: Create comprehensive README documentation with installation instructions, usage examples, architecture overview, and contribution guidelines.
acceptanceCriteria: README.md exists at project root with project title, description, and badges
Installation section covers: Python 3.11+ requirement, pip install, WeasyPrint system dependencies, Playwright setup, .env configuration
Usage section shows examples for: generating from file, generating from URL, searching job boards, specifying language and photo
Architecture section includes a text-based pipeline diagram and module descriptions
Configuration section documents all environment variables and their purposes
README is well-formatted Markdown with proper headings, code blocks, and a table of contents
userStories.notes: This is the last story. By this point all features should be complete. README should accurately reflect the final state of the project.
